questions.question: What is a probability function?
options: A rule that assigns outcomes to sample spaces
A function $P\colon\mathcal{F}\to[0,1]$ assigning probabilities to events and satisfying the axioms
A function that returns negative numbers for rare events and positive numbers for likely ones.
A list of all possible ordered selections

questions.question: What is the domain of the probability function?
options: The real line outside the sample space
The set of all factorials
$\mathcal{F}$, a collection of events

questions.question: What is the codomain of $P\colon\mathcal{F}\to[0,1]$?
options: $\mathcal{F}$
$\mathbb{N}$ only

questions.question: What does a probability function assign probabilities to?
options: Only informal statements outside the model
Only individual symbols with no sample space
Events
Only factorial expressions

questions.question: What does a probability function turn a sample space into?
options: A list with no event probabilities
A deterministic equation
A permutation count
A usable probability model

questions.question: For a fair die, what probability should a probability function assign to the event $\{1\}$?
For a fair six-sided die, let $S=\{1,2,3,4,5,6\}$ be the sample space. What is $P(S)$?
In a reliability model, which input is appropriate for a probability function?
options: The event that the system fails
The word reliability with no event
A negative probability value
The number of boxes in stars and bars

questions.question: For a deck of cards, which event might a probability function assign a probability to?
options: Drawing a heart
The factorial $52!$ by itself
The number $365$
A box with no sample space

questions.question: If $A$ and $B$ are disjoint events, how should a probability function handle $A\cup B$?
options: By multiplying $P(A)$ and $P(B)$ always
By adding $P(A)$ and $P(B)$
By assigning a negative value
By refusing to assign a probability

questions.question: Why must a probability function satisfy the axioms of probability?
options: To make every event equally likely
To make the assigned chances consistent with nonnegativity, certainty, and additivity
To ensure all sample spaces are finite
To force every event to have probability one, so that all the assigned chances are consistent.

questions.question: Which statement correctly distinguishes a sample space from a probability function?
options: The sample space assigns probabilities; the probability function lists outcomes
Both objects are always the same set
The sample space lists possible outcomes; the probability function assigns chances to events
The probability function exists before events are defined

questions.question: Why is the range $[0,1]$ natural for a probability function?
options: Probabilities cannot be negative and cannot exceed one
Events can contain only the numbers between zero and one
Sample spaces always equal $[0,1]$
Counting formulas always produce decimals

questions.question: A proposed probability function assigns $P(S)=0.8$, where $S$ is the full sample space. Which probability axiom does this assignment violate?
options: It violates the axiom that $P(S)=1$ for the whole sample space
It violates nonnegativity, because $P(S)=0.8$ is less than one
It violates no axiom, since $0.8$ lies between $0$ and $1$
It violates the axiom $P(\varnothing)=0$ for the empty event

questions.question: A proposed probability function assigns $P(A)=-0.2$ for an event $A$. What is wrong?
options: Negative probabilities are required for rare events
The event $A$ must be the sample space
The issue disappears if $A$ is disjoint from another event
Probabilities must lie in $[0,1]$

questions.question: For a fair die probability function, what is $P(\{1,2\})$?
Why is assigning probabilities only to events more precise than assigning them to informal sentences?
options: Events specify exactly which outcomes make the statement occur
Events are always single outcomes, so each has one probability
Events always have equally likely outcomes, so they can be counted
Events never overlap, so their probabilities can always be added

questions.question: The probability function $P\colon\mathcal{F}\to[0,1]$ is not defined on arbitrary subsets. Which role does $\mathcal{F}$ play?
options: It is the set of all numerical probability values
It is always the empty set
It specifies which events receive probabilities
It replaces the sample space with a factorial

questions.question: Suppose $A$ and $B$ are disjoint and a proposed probability function gives $P(A)=0.7$, $P(B)=0.5$. Why is this impossible if $A\cup B\subseteq S$?
options: The union would have probability $1.2$, exceeding $1$
Disjoint events must have equal probabilities
Each event must have probability zero
The sample space must have probability $2$

questions.question: A model has fair die outcomes. Which assignment is consistent with the stated examples?
options: $P(\{1\})=-1/6$ and all other faces have probability $1/6$
$P(\{i\})=1/6$ for each face $i=1,\ldots,6$
